title: A Songbook for the Vow
premise: After a hand tremor ends his career mid-concert, cellist Dominic Oyelaran retreats to his late grandmother's failing bakery in a small coastal town, hiding behind anonymous letters assigned by the community center's pen-pal program. His correspondent turns out to be Marisol Vega, the violinist whose testimony in an old conservatory dispute he blames for his downfall—and who has her own secret about that night. As their letters deepen into something neither can take back, and the bakery's lease deadline looms, Dominic must choose between protecting his grievance and claiming the found family, and the second chance, he swore he didn't believe in. The story ends with him performing again—not flawlessly, but honestly—at the bakery's reopening, with Marisol beside him.
about_author: Yara Winterbourne is a former orchestral librarian turned novelist who writes love stories set in the spaces where music and ordinary life collide. She lives in a coastal town much like the one in this book, where she claims the bakery on the corner inspired everything.

chapters.title: The Last Note That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Flashback to the catastrophic final performance—his hand seizing mid-solo, the silence, the walk offstage—interwoven with his arrival at his grandmother's shuttered bakery. He unpacks nothing, literally and emotionally. Emotional beat: grief disguised as practicality; he tells himself he's just 'managing the estate.'

chapters.title: Paper Strangers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The town community center runs a pen-pal program to combat winter isolation; his neighbor signs him up as a joke. He writes a deliberately hostile first letter to get removed from the list. Instead, his anonymous correspondent matches his sarcasm beat for beat. Emotional beat: reluctant spark—he's annoyed to be entertained.

chapters.title: Marisol, Measured in Flour
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. We meet the correspondent: a violinist teaching at the local school, rationing her savings, haunted by a decision she made at the conservatory years ago. She recognizes something wounded in her pen pal's anger because she recognizes it in herself. Emotional beat: guarded tenderness; she decides not to run.

chapters.title: Lease Terms
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A developer's letter gives the bakery ninety days: renew with back rent he doesn't have, or sell. The town offers help he refuses out of pride. His letters become the only place he admits fear. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; isolation starts costing more than it protects.

chapters.title: Duet, Unrehearsed
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A school fundraiser needs musicians; she asks the bakery to host and the recluse to play. Dominic refuses, but they argue their way into an accidental duet when she picks up a violin in his shop. Neither knows they've already met in letters. Emotional beat: music as involuntary honesty.

chapters.title: What the Letters Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both correspondents confess their worst nights—his collapse, her compromise—in writing while growing closer in person, each unaware the confidant and the companion are the same. Rising tension: near-misses of recognition, a shared joke landing twice. Emotional beat: intimacy built on a structural lie.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Marisol leaves a handwritten note at the bakery; the handwriting matches his pen pal's. He confronts her, and the old grievance detonates: she was the student who testified against him in the dispute he believes ended his career. Emotional beat: betrayal—the one safe thing becomes the wound.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She tells the whole truth: she defended him that night and was punished for it, blacklisted quietly, her career ending in a slower, quieter way than his. Her letters were never manipulation—they were how she survived staying. Emotional beat: devastating reversal; both were surviving the same crime.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the lease expiring, the town shows up anyway—students, neighbors, the community center—with a benefit concert at the bakery. Dominic must decide whether to play with a trembling hand in front of everyone, including Marisol, whom he hasn't forgiven or forgotten. Climax: he takes the stage; the tremor comes; he plays through it, imperfectly, and the room holds him.

chapters.title: A Songbook for the Vow
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing with a shared epilogue voice. The lease is renewed with community backing; the bakery reopens with a chalkboard menu and a corner for Sunday music. Dominic forgives the man in the mirror, then asks Marisol to stay—not as pen pals, but as partners. Final beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into; the vow is to stop disappearing.
